### 1) What is on the screen
The frame shows only the upper half of a wardroom interior on black. Top 0-100px is an orange-brown wood block wall with three round blue portholes, a white trim strip with a row of small yellow lamps, and brown deck below. The lower ~55% is flat black empty. The eye goes first to the center blue porthole around x110,y15,w20,h20 because it is the only saturated cool colour on warm orange. I cannot see a player, enemy, HUD, or objective — I cannot see what the player is being asked to do in this frame.

### 2) Does it look like a real NES game
(a) palette count reads as NES — PASS: measured 9 distinct colours, all in the 64-entry NES palette, well under the 25 colours on screen ceiling (12 BG + 12 sprite + 1 backdrop).
(b) shading is flat, one colour per shape — PASS: wall blocks, portholes, lamps are flat fills, no gradient banding visible.
(c) sprites read at a glance against background — FAIL: I cannot see any sprites in this frame, only background tiles; nothing to read as player/enemy/object.
(d) no anti-aliasing and no soft edges — PASS: edges on portholes, bricks and lamp row are hard 1px steps, no soft text/window borders visible.
(e) colour changes land on 16x16 grid — PASS in impression: wall / trim / floor bands are horizontal full-width strips, porthole housings sit in ~16px columns, no drifting attribute bleed I can see.

Measured numbers do not contradict the impression: 256 x 240, multiple of 8, 9 colours, 56.5% one colour matches the large black void I see.

### 3) Composition and text
Crowded on top, empty on bottom. The top 0-104px packs wall + trim + lamps + floor in four tight bands; the bottom x0,y104,w256,h136 is empty black. The focal point — blue portholes at top — is not where battle action would need to be, center-screen is void. I cannot see any text, HUD, dialogue box or window border in this frame. Text regions: none visible. Worst one: missing — at 256 x 240 you need at least an 8x8 glyph row for location/objective, and there is none.

### 4) What looks AI generated or off
Mostly handmade and honest tile work, not smeary AI art, but unfinished as a frame:
- composition reads as a background rip, not a designed shot: 56.5% black is dead space, not NES letterbox.
- detail without structure in the lamp row x60,y50,w136,h8: ~17 identical yellow blobs with no 16px spacing logic, more like a prompt for "lights" than placed tiles.
- side wall cutoff at right edge x240,y32,w16,h80 shows half-tiles chopped by screen edge, border is not a whole number of tiles.
- I cannot see pillow shading or gradients, but I also cannot see a floor table, chairs, or wardroom furniture the name promises.

### 5) Five concrete fixes
1. Fill the black void x0,y112,w256,h128: replace backdrop $0F black with tiled floor using BG palette $0F black / $07 dark brown / $17 light brown / $28 tan, on a strict 16 x 16 attribute grid, add a 64x32 table centered at x96,y160,w64,h32.
2. Fix the lamp strip x56,y48,w144,h8: delete to 8 lamps, one per 16px cell starting at x64, redraw each as 8x8 tile $28 yellow center + $0F outline, all in same BG palette to respect 16 x 16 change rule, move row up 8px to y40.
3. Re-seat the three portholes x16,y12,w32,h32 / x112,y12,w32,h32 / x200,y12,w32,h32: snap each housing to 16x16, redraw white highlight as 2x2px square $30 white in top-left of blue $12, remove 1px gray fringe.
4. Add ceiling shadow band x0,y0,w256,h16: insert 16px high strip using $06 dark red-brown over $16 light red to separate ceiling from wall, aligned to 8x8 tiles, no partial tiles.
5. Add HUD text row x8,y8,w240,h8: draw "WARDROOM" in 8x8 white $30 on $0F, left-aligned on the 8px glyph grid, capitals only, to give focal point and legibility test at 256 x 240.

### 6) Scores and machine readable block
nes_authenticity: 7 - colours and tiles legal, but half-frame empty fails shipped-game test.
readability: 4 - top reads, bottom has no play space, no text.
charm: 5 - warm wood + blue portholes nice, killed by void.
